message.reasoning:
We need to analyze method removeRecord. It does:

public boolean removeRecord(Record r, int section) {
    Section.check(section);
    if ((sections[section] != null) && sections[section].remove(r)) {
        header.decCount(section);
        return true;
    } else {
        return false;
    }
}

Potential exception scenarios:

- Section.check throws IllegalArgumentException for invalid section values (including negative, out of range, maybe SECTION.QUESTION not allowed? Need to see Section.check implementation. Usually Section.check ensures section is >=0 && <=3 (QUESTION, ANSWER, AUTHORITY, ADDITIONAL). Might also reject QUESTION because removal not allowed? Not sure. But existing test case expects IllegalArgumentException when section 0 (QUESTION) is passed. So Section.check throws IllegalArgumentException for SECTION.QUESTION.

- Null pointer: if r is null, sections[section].remove(r) will call List.remove(null). List.remove(null) removes first null element if present, else returns false; it does not throw NPE. However if sections[section] is null, then we don't call remove. So NPE may not be thrown. But existing test case expects NullPointerException thrown when passing null Record. However List.remove(null) does not throw NPE; but maybe sections[section] is a List that does not allow null (maybe ArrayList allows null). So maybe the code earlier may cause NPE elsewhere? Actually header.decCount(section) may be called only if removal succeeded; header may be null? header is always non-null after Message creation? Not guaranteed. Could be null if not set? In Message constructors, header is initialized. Assuming not null.

Potential exception: If sections array is null or uninitialized, accessing sections[section] could throw NPE. But sections is always initialized in constructor to new List[Section.MAX]; but not sure.

Maybe IllegalStateException if header is null? Not typical.

Also possible IndexOutOfBoundsException if section index is out of bounds before Section.check? Section.check likely checks range, but if Section.check is not called (e.g., if we pass null for sections array?), still we call Section.check first.

Thus exception scenarios:

1. IllegalArgumentException from Section.check for invalid section values: negative, > max, or SECTION.QUESTION (0). Already covered.

2. NullPointerException if Record r is null and sections[section] is non-null and its remove method throws NPE (unlikely). But we can still include test case.

3. NullPointerException if sections array itself is null (maybe via reflection). But not typical usage.

4. IllegalStateException if header is null and decCount is called after successful removal. Could happen if Message constructed without header? In Message default constructor, header = new Header(); but maybe after calling setHeader(null) we could set header null. So removal that succeeds would cause NPE when header.decCount called. That's an exception scenario: NPE (or maybe NullPointerException) when header is null.

Thus we need to add test cases for:

- header null scenario: add record, then setHeader(null) (if setter exists; setHeader(Header h) is present). Then removeRecord that matches should cause NullPointerException.

- sections array null scenario: maybe via reflection set sections = null, then call removeRecord with valid section; Section.check passes; then sections[section] throws NPE. Could be considered.

- sections[section] list is present but contains null elements; removal of null record may cause NPE? Actually List.remove(null) works.

We also need to avoid duplication with existing cases. Existing cases cover invalid sections, null record, empty list, list without record, successful removal, duplicate, equality, etc.

Missing exception scenarios: header null leading to NPE, sections array null leading to NPE, maybe IllegalArgumentException for section being QUESTION (already covered). Also maybe IllegalArgumentException for section being out of range (already covered). So we add two new groups: one for header null, one for sections null.

We can create group "Message.removeRecord.headerNull" and "Message.removeRecord.sectionsNull".

- Setup: Create Message, add a record to ANSWER section, then setHeader(null). Then call removeRecord(record, Section.ANSWER). Expect NullPointerException (or maybe IllegalStateException). The code will call sections[section].remove(r) returns true, then header.decCount(section) triggers NPE because header is null. So expected NullPointerException.

Case description: Removing a record when header is null should result in NullPointerException due to decCount call.

Case 2: sections array null scenario:

- Use reflection to set private field sections to null (or maybe use a subclass). Then call removeRecord with valid section and any record. Section.check passes, then sections[section] throws NPE. Expected NullPointerException.

But existing test expects NPE for null record, maybe they assume sections not null. We could add case where sections[section] is null and record null, expecting false (no exception). That is an edge case not covered.

Thus add group "Message.removeRecord.nullRecordEmptySection".
